subject: Chupa Chups
prose:
**Chupa Chups** is ultimately owned by **Perfetti Van Melle Group B.V.**, a privately held Italian-Dutch confectionery company headquartered in Schiphol-Oost, Netherlands (with additional corporate roots in Lainate, Italy).

### Key ownership chain

- **Chupa Chups**, the iconic Spanish lollipop brand founded in 1958 by Enric Bernat, was acquired by Perfetti Van Melle in July 2006.
- **Perfetti Van Melle** was formed in 2001 through the merger of Italy's Perfetti SpA and the Netherlands' Van Melle Group B.V.
- Perfetti Van Melle is a **family-owned** company, controlled by the **Perfetti family** — notably brothers **Augusto Perfetti** and **Giorgio Perfetti**, sons of co-founder Ambrogio Perfetti. The company remains privately held and is not publicly listed.

Perfetti Van Melle is one of the world's largest confectionery groups, also owning brands such as Mentos, Fruittella, Smint, Airheads, and Alpenliebe, with operations in over 150 countries.

subject: Freixenet
prose:
## Ultimate Ownership of Freixenet

**Freixenet S.A.**, the Spanish cava producer founded in 1928, is ultimately owned by the **Oetker family** — specifically by **Dr. Alfred Oetker** and **Ferdinand Oetker** — through the following chain:

1. **Oetker Collection KG** (formerly part of the broader Oetker Group) is the ultimate parent company of Freixenet S.A.
2. **Henkell & Co. Sektkellerei KG** (based in Wiesbaden, Germany) is the direct parent of Freixenet S.A.
3. The group operates under the brand name **Henkell Freixenet**, which is the world's leading sparkling wine producer.

### Key milestones:
- In **2018**, Henkell & Co. (part of the Oetker Group) acquired an initial ~50.67% stake in Freixenet, with the founding Ferrer and Bonet families retaining the rest.
- In **2021**, the Oetker Group was split among family branches. Henkell Freixenet was placed under **Geschwister Oetker Beteiligungen KG** (now Oetker Collection KG), controlled by the three younger Oetker siblings: Dr. Alfred Oetker, Carl Ferdinand Oetker, and Julia Johanna Oetker.
- Subsequently, Henkell Freixenet acquired the **remaining shares** from the Ferrer Family and José Luis Bonet, making it the **sole shareholder** of Freixenet S.A.

In summary, Freixenet is 100% owned by Henkell Freixenet, which in turn belongs to **Oetker Collection KG**, a privately held German conglomerate owned by members of the Oetker family.

subject: Estrella Damm
prose:
## Ownership of Estrella Damm

**Estrella Damm** is a Spanish lager beer brand manufactured by **Sociedad Anónima Damm (S.A. Damm)**, a brewery headquartered in Barcelona, founded in 1910.

S.A. Damm is ultimately controlled by the **Carceller family**. The family's connection to Damm dates back to the 1970s, when Josepa Coll (grandmother of the current leader) acquired a stake in the company. Today, the family holds its interest through several vehicles:

- **Seegrund BV**, a Dutch holding company, owns approximately **16.3%** of Damm's capital.
- **Grupo DISA**, the Canary Islands–based energy group also controlled by the Carcellers, holds around **33%** of Damm.

Together, these give the Carceller family roughly **49%** of Damm's share capital, making them the dominant shareholders.

**Demetrio Carceller Arce** has served as executive chairman and CEO of Damm since 1994. He was recognised with the Forbes Best CEO 2024 award for transforming Damm "from a traditional family business into a modern, high-quality company." Other board members include representatives of the German **Oetker family** (Rudolf-August Oetker) and other long-standing partners.

In short, Estrella Damm is ultimately owned by the **Carceller family** through S.A. Damm, with Demetrio Carceller Arce at the helm.

subject: Cola Cao
prose:
**Cola Cao** is a Spanish cocoa-based powdered drink brand, launched in 1945. It is manufactured by **Idilia Foods, S.L.**, a Spanish food company headquartered in Barcelona.

### Ownership chain

- **Cola Cao** → manufactured by **Idilia Foods**
- **Idilia Foods** is privately owned by the **Ferrero Jordi family**.

Idilia Foods was born in 2015 from the split of **Nutrexpa**, a food group co-founded in 1940s Barcelona by José Ignacio Ferrero Cabanach and José María Ventura Mallofré. When the two founding families decided to divide the business for succession purposes (a project they called "Friends Forever"), the **Ferrero family** retained the cocoa and chocolate brands — Cola Cao, Nocilla, Okey, and Paladín — under the new entity Idilia Foods, while the **Ventura family** took the biscuit and other food brands under Adam Foods.

The board of Idilia Foods has been led by the five Ferrero Jordi siblings — Ignasi (president), Javier (CEO), Antoni, Núria, and Nadet — with the third generation of the family also joining the board in recent years.

So the **ultimate owners of Cola Cao are the Ferrero Jordi family**, through their private company Idilia Foods.

subject: Mercadona
prose:
## Mercadona — Ultimate Ownership

**Mercadona SA** is a privately held, family-owned Spanish supermarket chain founded on 18 January 1977. It is ultimately owned and controlled by the **Roig family**, specifically:

- **Juan Roig** — Chairman, CEO, and majority shareholder, holding approximately **50.66%** of Mercadona's shares. He took control of the company in 1981 after buying out other family members.
- **Hortensia Herrero** — Juan Roig's wife and Vice President of Mercadona, who owns approximately **27.71%** of the shares (held through her investment vehicle Herrecha Inversiones).
- **Fernando Roig** — Juan Roig's brother, who controls around **9%** of the shares through his company Portovan SL. Fernando is also known as the owner of Villarreal football club.

Together, the Roig family holds the entirety of Mercadona's equity. Juan Roig and Hortensia Herrero have four daughters — **Carolina, Hortensia, Amparo, and Juana** — all of whom sit on Mercadona's board of directors. Juana Roig, the youngest, leads Mercadona's digital division (Mercadona Tech) and has been widely identified as a potential successor to her father.

In summary, **Juan Roig is the ultimate controlling owner** of Mercadona, with his wife Hortensia Herrero as the second-largest shareholder.

subject: Nutella
prose:
**Nutella** is a chocolate and hazelnut spread introduced in 1964 by the **Ferrero Group**. It is manufactured by **Ferrero S.p.A.**, an Italian confectionery company headquartered in Casalgrasso (province of Cuneo), Italy.

The Ferrero Group is a **privately held company** fully owned by the **Ferrero family**. **Giovanni Ferrero** serves as executive chairman and majority owner. The family has maintained full private ownership of the group since its founding — there is no public listing or outside controlling shareholder.

In short, the ultimate owner of Nutella is **Giovanni Ferrero and the Ferrero family**, through their private ownership of the Ferrero Group.

subject: Oreo
prose: **Oreo** is a chocolate sandwich cookie brand that was launched in 1912 and originally created by Nabisco. Today, Oreo is manufactured and owned by **Mondelez International, Inc.**, a global food and beverage company headquartered in Chicago. Mondelez International is a publicly traded corporation (it was established in 2013 when it was spun off from Kraft Foods) and serves as the ultimate parent company behind the Oreo brand.

subject: Zara
prose:
## Who Owns Zara?

**Zara** is the flagship brand of **Inditex (Industria de Diseño Textil, S.A.)**, a Spanish multinational fast-fashion retailer headquartered in Arteixo, Spain, founded in 1985.

### Ownership chain

- **Amancio Ortega** founded both Zara (in 1975) and Inditex. He remains the ultimate controlling owner through his investment vehicle **Pontegadea Inversiones SL**, a Spanish asset-management and real-estate firm he founded in 2001 in A Coruña.
- **Pontegadea Inversiones** is a major investor in Inditex and serves as the holding company through which Ortega channels his stake.
- Inditex is publicly listed, but the Ortega family — via Pontegadea and related entities such as **Partler Participaciones, S.L.U.** — holds the controlling interest.

### Current leadership

Amancio Ortega's daughter, **Marta Ortega Pérez**, serves as non-executive chairperson of Inditex.

In short, **Amancio Ortega** is the ultimate owner of Zara, holding his controlling stake in Inditex through Pontegadea Inversiones.

subject: IKEA
prose:
## Who Ultimately Owns IKEA?

IKEA has a multi-layered ownership structure, but at the very top sits the **Inter IKEA Foundation**, a Liechtenstein-registered foundation headquartered in Vaduz. Its mission is to secure the independence and longevity of the IKEA Concept.

Here is how the structure works:

- **Inter IKEA Foundation** is the ultimate owner of the **Inter IKEA Group**, which owns the IKEA brand, concept, and franchise system through **Inter IKEA Holding B.V.**
- **Inter IKEA Holding B.V.** (based in the Netherlands) sits beneath the foundation and controls the entities that manage the IKEA trademark and supply chain (including **Inter IKEA Systems B.V.**, the franchisor).
- Separately, the **INGKA Foundation** (a Dutch foundation) owns **INGKA Holding**, which operates the vast majority of IKEA stores worldwide as the largest IKEA franchisee. The INGKA Foundation is the world's largest charitable foundation by some measures.
- There is also the **Interogo Foundation**, another Liechtenstein-based entity historically linked to the Kamprad family, which has had a role in the ownership chain.

IKEA was founded by **Ingvar Kamprad**, who deliberately transferred ownership into these foundation structures to remove direct family control, avoid potential conflicts of interest, and ensure the long-term survival of the IKEA brand. Because IKEA is owned by private foundations rather than being publicly traded, it has no shareholders in the traditional sense.

**In short:** The Inter IKEA Foundation is the ultimate custodian of the IKEA brand and concept, while the INGKA Foundation owns the entity that operates most IKEA stores.

subject: Nespresso
prose:
**Nespresso** (formally **Nestlé Nespresso SA**) is a wholly owned subsidiary of **Nestlé S.A.**, the Swiss multinational food and beverage corporation headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland. Nestlé has been Nespresso's parent company since the brand's inception in the early 1980s, making Nestlé the ultimate owner of Nespresso.

Nestlé S.A. is a publicly traded company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange, so its ownership is in turn distributed among public shareholders.

subject: Ben & Jerry's
prose:
**Ben & Jerry's** was founded by Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield, who sold the company to **Unilever** in 2000 for $326 million. Unilever owned Ben & Jerry's for over two decades.

In 2025, Unilever spun off its entire ice cream division — including Ben & Jerry's — into a separate publicly traded company called **Magnum Corporation**. So as of now, **Magnum Corporation** (the spun-off ice cream business formerly part of Unilever) is the ultimate owner of Ben & Jerry's.

Co-founders Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield no longer have ownership control. Both have publicly called on Magnum Corporation to sell Ben & Jerry's to "socially aligned investors," citing concerns that the parent company has restricted the brand's social advocacy mission.

subject: Red Bull
prose:
## Red Bull GmbH — Ultimate Ownership

**Red Bull GmbH** is an Austrian beverage and media company founded in 1987 by **Dietrich Mateschitz** (Austria) and **Chaleo Yoovidhya** (Thailand). Ownership has always been split between the two founding families:

### Current ownership structure

| Shareholder | Stake | Vehicle |
|---|---|---|
| **Yoovidhya family** | ~49% | TC Agro Trading Company (Hong Kong) |
| **Mateschitz family (Mark Mateschitz)** | ~49% | Distribution & Marketing GmbH (Austria) |

- **Chalerm Yoovidhya**, Chaleo's eldest son, previously held an additional personal 2% stake (giving the Yoovidhya side a combined 51% majority). That personal stake has since been sold, bringing the two families' holdings to parity.
- After **Dietrich Mateschitz's death in October 2022**, his son **Mark Mateschitz** inherited the family's 49% stake by April 2023.
- After **Chaleo Yoovidhya's death in 2012**, his share passed to his eldest son **Chalerm Yoovidhya**, who heads the group. Chalerm's brother **Saravoot Yoovidhya** serves as managing director of Red Bull Thailand.

In summary, Red Bull is ultimately owned in roughly equal halves by the **Yoovidhya family** of Thailand and the **Mateschitz family** of Austria.

subject: Moleskine
prose:
**Moleskine** (Moleskine S.r.l.), the Italian notebook and stationery company headquartered in Milan, is ultimately owned by **D'Ieteren Group**, a Belgian company headquartered in Brussels. D'Ieteren Group is both the direct and ultimate parent of Moleskine.

D'Ieteren Group acquired a controlling 41% stake in Moleskine in September 2016 from private equity investors Syntegra Capital and Index Ventures for €2.40 per share (valuing the company at approximately €506 million), and subsequently launched a mandatory tender offer for the remaining shares. D'Ieteren Group itself is a family-controlled company, founded in 1805 by the D'Ieteren family. Its other major holdings include Belron (a global leader in vehicle glass repair, known for brands like Carglass, Autoglass, and Safelite) and D'Ieteren Automotive (a car distributor in Belgium for brands such as Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, and others).

subject: Telepizza
prose:
## Telepizza — Ultimate Ownership

Telepizza is a Spanish pizza delivery company founded in 1987 and headquartered in San Sebastián de los Reyes, Madrid. The group now operates under the name **Food Delivery Brands S.A.** (rebranded from Grupo Telepizza in 2020) and runs the Telepizza, Pizza Hut, Jeno's Pizza, and Apache Pizza brands across multiple markets.

### Ownership history

- **2006:** Permira led an €850 million take-private of Telepizza.
- **2014:** KKR acquired a 36% stake for €180 million as part of a refinancing deal.
- **2016:** Telepizza was re-listed on the Madrid stock exchange via an IPO, with Permira and KKR selling down their stakes.
- **2018–2019:** KKR launched a takeover bid at €6 per share, eventually acquiring a controlling 56.29% stake and delisting the company. KKR later raised its stake to approximately 83.96%, with co-investors Torreal, Artá Capital, and Safra Group also holding positions.

### Current ownership (since January 2024)

Following financial difficulties, Food Delivery Brands underwent a **debt restructuring** through a Spanish restructuring plan that closed in **January 2024**. The restructuring involved the capitalisation of 67% of the company's €335 million in existing bonds and a €60 million capital injection under a new €100 million facility.

As a result, the **noteholders acquired full control** of the company, diluting previous shareholders including KKR. The new controlling owners are a group of institutional investors led by:

- **Oak Hill Advisors**
- **Fortress Investment Group**
- **Blantyre Capital**
- **H.I.G. Capital**

These four firms, which held more than 70% of the company's bonds, are now the ultimate owners of Telepizza / Food Delivery Brands.

subject: Casa Tarradellas
prose:
**Casa Tarradellas** is a **family-owned** Spanish food company. It is managed by **Josep Terradellas Arcarons**, who runs the business. Founded in 1976, the company is headquartered in Gurb, Barcelona, Spain.

Casa Tarradellas is privately held and remains under the control of the **Terradellas family** — there is no external corporate or private-equity parent. The company is a market leader in Spain across categories such as pizza, fresh dough, charcuterie, sandwiches, and pâté, and recorded approximately €859 million in sales in Spain in a recent year.

Notably, Casa Tarradellas also acquired full ownership of **Herta Foods** after purchasing Nestlé's remaining 40% stake, completing a process that began in 2019 when Nestlé divested 60% of its Herta charcuterie and dough business to form a joint venture with Casa Tarradellas.
